AI / HUMAN REVIEW01

Survey Audio Intelligence & ML Audit Assist

Early evaluation2026–present

Helping human reviewers find evidence in Hindi/Hinglish survey audio through transcription, speaker diarization, and structured audit signals.

7 audios evaluated · ~30% of auditor work prefilledEarly test result; prefill coverage, not validated accuracy or measured time saved.
PythonASRAudio processing
My contribution & approach +

My contribution

Building the pipeline end to end: audio processing, chunked speech recognition, speaker diarization, evidence extraction, and audit-signal evaluation.

Human judgment stays in the workflow

Validation focuses on transcription errors, speaker attribution, critical answer evidence, and audit outcomes. Final disposition stays within the existing CRM workflow. Tests on seven audios suggest roughly 30% of auditor work can be prefilled; broader evaluation is still needed.

What I’m working toward

Improve prefill accuracy and expand coverage across questions. Longer term, explore whether some samples can safely skip manual audit once evaluation supports that decision. Audit elimination is a goal, not an achieved result.

FIELD NOTES

What I’m learning to ask.

Selected reflections from product discussions, technical sessions, and reading.

01PRODUCT METRICSMore usage is not always a better outcome.Start with the job, the user’s choice, and the decision a metric will inform.+

What changed my thinking

A mandatory operations tool can have high usage even when the experience is poor. A planning tool used once a week can be valuable without strong daily activity. The same dashboard cannot tell both stories.

The lens I’d use

First establish who uses the product, who pays, what job it performs, and how it gets adopted. For an operations workflow, I’d look at completion, errors, and time per task. For weekly planning, I’d look at weekly completion and whether plans are ready when needed.

Less time in a tool can be a good outcome when it removes repetitive work. More time can also be valuable when the task calls for deeper engagement. The task determines the interpretation.

The question I keepWhat decision would change if this metric moved?

Product learning discussion · 14 July; product-context notes

02PRODUCT CRAFTA PRD should make the next decision easier.Clarity comes from visible requirements and edge cases, not document length.+

The lesson

When every detail has equal weight, the important requirements are easy to miss. A useful PRD gives engineering, design, and QA a shared understanding of the problem and expected behavior.

What deserves the space

The problem, why it matters, the scope, important edge cases, and how success will be assessed. Supporting detail should help someone make or verify a decision.

Connection to my work

The failed-submission form fix is a concrete example: preserve entered values when the API rejects the request; reset only after success. That distinction gives implementation and QA a clear behavior to work toward.

The question I keepCan the team identify the expected behavior and its failure paths in one reading?

Product learning discussion · 14 July

03TECHNICAL PRODUCTA smaller image is not the same as a faster release.Separate deployment efficiency, build time, and the experience users actually feel.+

The distinction that stayed with me

The session discussed reducing container size with multi-stage builds and improving build time through reuse. They address different parts of delivery: removing build-only dependencies from runtime does not automatically make the build itself faster.

What this changes for a PM

I’d ask which delay we are solving: building the application, deploying it, or loading it for a user. Each needs its own measurement. An infrastructure improvement should not automatically become a claim about user experience.

Trade-offs matter too. Caching brings freshness questions; lazy loading introduces loading states. Release planning also needs a way to observe product health and recover when something breaks.

The question I keepWhat gets faster, how will we measure it, and how do we recover safely?

DevOps learning exchange · 11 August 2026

04READING → PRACTICEThe feature is only part of the product.My takeaway from Zero to One and The Lean Product Playbook: solve a specific problem and plan for adoption.+

Two ideas I connect

From Zero to One, I take the question of meaningful differentiation: what becomes easier for the customer? From The Lean Product Playbook, I take the discipline of defining the customer and unmet need before committing to a solution.

How I think about AI cleaning

The useful starting point is the effort involved in cleaning subjective survey responses. AI is a possible way to address that work; its presence alone does not establish value.

My responsibilities in the live workflow include requirements, wireframes, QA, adoption, and improvements after adoption. That makes the adoption question concrete: delivery is followed by changing project requirements and continued product work.

The question I keepWhat is the smallest workflow that can demonstrate value, and what will help people keep using it?

Reading reflections · Zero to One, Peter Thiel with Blake Masters; The Lean Product Playbook, Dan Olsen
